gutshot_check: Architect's gutshot claim is WRONG. A9 on Jh7h2c has NO gutshot. Enumerate straights containing A or 9 with the board cards available: (a) 5-6-7-8-9 needs runner-runner 5+6+8; (b) 6-7-8-9-T needs runner-runner 6+8+T; (c) 7-8-9-T-J — board has 7,J + hero 9, needs 8 AND T = runner-runner straight draw, NOT a gutshot (gutshot = one card completes); (d) 8-9-T-J-Q needs runner-runner 8+T+Q; (e) 9-T-J-Q-K needs runner-runner T+Q+K; (f) A-2-3-4-5 wheel — board has 2, needs runner-runner 3+4+5; (g) T-J-Q-K-A needs runner-runner T+Q+K. No single card on the turn makes hero a straight. Hero has NUT FD only (9 outs) plus A overcard (3 dirty outs) — combo-draw value ~9-10 clean outs, NOT the 13-14 outs architect's combo-draw framing implies. This materially weakens the semi-bluff RAISE case.
reasoning: GTO-theoretic frame: SB OOP nut-flush draw on 2-tone board in 5-way pot, facing CO bet (32%) + BTN cold-call, with UTG and MP still un-acted behind. The architect's RAISE-primary recommendation rests on three claims, two of which fail under scrutiny. First, the 'combo-draw monster' framing requires a gutshot that does not exist — hero has 9 nut-flush outs and ~3 dirty overcard outs (As blocker irrelevant since hero holds Ah), not 13-14 outs. Raw flop equity vs a tight Jx-or-better bet-and-call defending range is ~32-38%, not the architect's 45-48%. Second, the fold-equity calculus from CO/BTN is poor: CO open-bet into 4 villains multiway has a value-heavy distribution (Jx+, overpairs, sets, occasional better FDs with Kh/Qh), and BTN's flat with one street invested commits him to Jx-or-better. A check-raise to 16bb (4x) into 20.5bb prices CO/BTN in cheaply with any pair+FD or Jx+; fold equity from them is structurally low in multiway bet-and-call chains. Third, UTG/MP fold equity is real but already realized — they checked and now face a bet+call+raise, so their continuation rate is near zero regardless of whether hero raises 3x or 5x. Conversely, the CALL line is dominated: hero needs 16.3% equity, has ~33%+ raw with implied odds for the nut flush (highest-EV one-card draw on the board), and keeps capped UTG/MP in for stack extraction when the flush hits. OOP position penalty for raising is severe: bloating the pot OOP with a draw against ranges that won't fold means hero plays a large turn pot OOP without initiative when the heart misses (66% of the time). Solver-aligned baseline on bet-and-call-faced flops in 5-way SB-OOP with NFD strongly skews to CALL; CHECK-RAISE appears as a low-frequency mix (~15-25%) for blocker-rich combos, not the modal action. Verdict: CALL primary, MIX with CHECK-RAISE at low frequency.
